note: symmetric KV cache (q8_0/q8_0), NOT asymmetric — on OpenCL/Adreno asymmetric K/V cache silently breaks Flash Attention and falls back to CPU (25x slower) with no error in logs
_required_env: CRITICAL, verified 2026-08-01 bake-off: llama-server MUST be launched with LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$HOME:/system/lib64:/vendor/lib64:$PREFIX/opt/vendor/lib:$HOME/llama.cpp/build/bin" (same as bin/start-translation-server.sh) or OpenCL silently fails to find the Adreno platform ('ggml_opencl: platform IDs not available', -ngl is then silently ignored) and it falls back to slow 4-thread CPU-only inference with NO error surfaced anywhere except that one log line. Confirmed empirically: without this env var, generation was 6.6-7.2 tok/s; with it, 16.3 tok/s (better than the deep-research projection of 10-14 tok/s) and prompt eval went from 9.5 to 230.4 tok/s. Resident RSS also dropped from ~2.1GB to ~292MB once weights actually offloaded to GPU memory.
_endpoint_note: REVISED 2026-08-01 (second correction after the first response_format fix): use /v1/chat/completions with real system/user messages, NOT the raw /completion endpoint that common/mqm_review.py uses for Hy-MT2. Verified the difference matters: on the exact brace-heavy eve/agent-config.md code example, raw /completion with a fake 'System: ...' text prefix (even with json_schema forcing valid structure) consistently produced garbled, non-specific content ('missing code or code spans or spans', 21-27 tokens, reproducible across 4 different temperature/seed combinations -- not sampling noise) regardless of n_predict budget. The SAME case through /v1/chat/completions with proper system/user roles and response_format produced correct, specific, detailed output every time (3/3 seeds). Root cause: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct is chat-template-tuned (confirmed via /props: chat_template present) and mqm_review.py's raw-completion pattern is specifically suited to Hy-MT2, which is NOT chat-tuned (bare completion-style MT model, no chat template) -- the two models are not interchangeable in serving style despite both being served by the same llama-server binary. prompts/fact_drift.md and translation_hostile.md now have explicit '## System' / '## User' sections for this reason -- split on that heading when loading the template, do not send the whole file as one blob.
_response_format_note: Send this whole object as the `response_format` field in the /v1/chat/completions request body (llama-server grammar-constrained decoding via OpenAI-style json_schema wrapper). `minLength: 30` on `issue` matters -- without it the model produces terse, low-detail text (e.g. "Version numbers have changed.") instead of citing the specific differing values; the prompt's explicit "quote exact values" instruction is the other half of that fix and must stay in prompts/*.md.
_key_order_note: Verified 2026-08-01: the model's actual output key order follows the ORDER PROPERTIES ARE DECLARED in the schema, not the model's free choice -- tested both ways (issue-first schema -> issue-first output; severity-first schema -> severity-first output) on the same prompt/seed. This is a grammar-level guarantee, not probabilistic. The deep-research brief's 'issue before severity acts as embedded chain-of-thought' recommendation is preserved by construction because `issue` is declared before `severity` above -- do not reorder these two properties without re-testing whether judgment quality changes.
_prefill_note: The old {"issue": " prompt-prefill trick (from before json_schema/response_format was adopted) is REDUNDANT and, if code concatenates prefill+content the way an earlier design assumed, ACTIVELY BREAKS output -- grammar-constrained decoding regenerates a complete, self-contained JSON object from scratch regardless of any partial-JSON text already at the end of the prompt. Do NOT prefill the prompt/messages with partial JSON. Read `choices[0].message.content` from the /v1/chat/completions response directly as the complete JSON string -- no parser, no concatenation, no truncation logic needed at all.
_content_quality_caveat: IMPORTANT, verified 2026-08-01, NOT fully resolved. Sample size is SMALL -- be precise about this, don't overstate: JSON structure was validated across several seeded trials (all clean), but the single unseeded (default-random-seed) combined run of the FINAL prompt files is N=1 per prompt, not a large sample. That one run showed two distinct, structurally-valid-but-content-flawed results: (1) fact_drift -- severity stayed correct (3) but the issue text misquoted the specific new value in a garbled, self-contradictory sentence (repeated '4.8' fragments instead of citing the actual new value); (2) translation_hostile -- correctly detected THAT an idiom was present, but quoted the LITERAL EXAMPLE PHRASE from the prompt's own few-shot example ('easy peasy') instead of the real idiom in the input ('piece of cake'/'you are golden'), and severity dropped from a correct 3 (seeded run) to 1. Classification against three axes (false-negative drift-miss / false-positive phantom-drift / stylistic-only drift): NEITHER observed failure was a false negative -- the top-level verdict (issue exists, roughly this severity) was directionally right both times. NOT tested at all on the final config: a true clean/no-drift case (false-positive risk unverified post-chat-endpoint-switch -- a real gap, add to the Stage 9 regression set). What actually varied was accuracy of the SPECIFIC QUOTED EVIDENCE, not the top-level verdict -- worse than pure style drift (a wrong quote can mislead a reviewer) but recoverable because the UI shows source_excerpt/humanized_excerpt alongside issue text, so a human can cross-check the quote against the real paragraph. Fixed seeds WERE used during this investigation (seed=10/11/12) purely for reproducibility while diagnosing, not adopted in this config for production -- a fixed seed would make a bad output for a given paragraph deterministically-always-bad rather than reducing how often bad output occurs, and there is no retry-on-suspicious-output logic to pair it with (open question for Stage 9, not decided here). This is a real, unresolved quality ceiling of a 3B model on this task, not a bug to patch away -- it reinforces (does not undermine) the human-review gate already core to this design: book_editor_flags.json entries are proposals a human approves or discards, never auto-applied.
